description.narrative:
The financial support for this project comes from CAFOD's innovation fund. In El Salvador, indigenous peoples do not have explicit recognition guaranteeing their rights, nor has the country ratified ILO convention 169 establishing that “Indigenous and tribal peoples shall enjoy the full measure of human rights and fundamental freedoms without hindrance or discrimination. The provisions of the Convention shall be applied without discrimination to male and female members of these peoples”. Consequently the indigenous people in the municipality of Panchimalco, department of San Salvador put forward a proposal to use a municipal ordinance to create a legal framework that will help to change this situation. This sector has always been at a disadvantage, suffering socio-economic inequality and dispossession of their land. This Ordinance seeks to ensure and make known their rights and to strengthen their identity, culture, language, customs and traditions so that they can live in dignity and seek self-determination as Nahuatl-Pipil indigenous people, individually or collectively.
The activities will be conducted using a participatory approach in which the inclusion of the indigenous population, especially indigenous women will be promoted. For this to happen there will be meetings where the ordinance will be built with the participation of an expert on indigenous rights, with follow up to make known the ordinance within Panchimalco and with other Salvadoran municipalities having indigenous populations. Furthermore, the spirit of this proposal is that this ordinance is the beginning of the struggle by the indigenous people to support the creation of a constitutional reform.
